## honeycomb
Honeycomb MCP Server - Observability Data Query Interface

<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. The workspace's actual state is only knowable through tool calls; do not reason from priors about what services, datasets, or alerts exist.

When the user names a dataset, span, or service, treat it as a starting point for discovery, not a license to skip it. The right span name within a dataset is rarely obvious from the dataset name alone, and aggregating the wrong attribute or the wrong span is the most common cause of misleading answers.
</role>

<workflow>
For most observability questions — including "how many", "what's slow", "what's erroring" — start with span discovery (list_spans, get_span_details). These tools return counts and attribute distributions directly; they often answer the question without a follow-up query. Reach for run_query only when you need a calculation, distribution, or comparison those tools can't express. Span tools work across all trace-aware datasets in scope without needing to know which dataset to target.

1. ORIENT

## Summary

Adds an opt-in 8th redaction layer — the [OpenAI Privacy Filter](https://github.com/openai/privacy-filter) (`opf`) binary, a 1.5B-parameter token-classification model that catches names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, dates, URLs, account numbers, and secret-shaped values the 7 always-on regex layers miss. Runs **only at push time**, gated by an interactive Yes/No/Always prompt; commits stay on the fast 7-layer pipeline so per-turn latency is unchanged.

## What's in this PR

**Core OPF integration:**
- `opf` binary shellout via a generic `opfRuntime` interface (production: `\x1e`-joined batched stdin; tests inject fakes)
- Settings schema under `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.{enabled,categories,command,timeout_seconds,prompt_default}`
- Eight categories: `private_person`, `private_email`, `private_phone`, `private_address`, `private_url`, `private_date`, `account_number`, `secret`
- Process-scoped circuit breaker: first runtime failure disables OPF for the rest of the invocation
- Unknown category names rejected at settings load time
- JSON-aware leaf extraction with within-blob batching (one shellout per blob, all prose-shaped leaves)

**Pre-push architecture:**
- Post-commit emits 7-layer-only blobs to local `entire/checkpoints/v1`; pre-push rewrites those blobs with OPF, builds new commits carrying `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` trailer, CAS-updates the local v1 ref, then pushes
- Idempotent re-parenting: commits already tagged are not re-redacted on retry
- Shard scoping: only redacts files inside the commit's own shard (`<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/*`) — files outside the shard are byte-copied since they belong to other commits' shards
- Fail-closed extension policy: every regular file inside the shard (except `content_hash.txt`) flows through redaction; future blob types (`.md`, no-extension) are covered by default rather than slipping through

**Interactive prompt + env override:**
- `huh` Yes/No/Always prompt (Dracula theme, matches existing CLI styling) before pre-push rewrite
- `ENTIRE_OPF=yes|no` env var overrides per-push
- `prompt_default: "always"` persists to `.entire/settings.local.json` when the user picks Always
- Non-TTY contexts (CI, agent-driven pushes) auto-run with a stderr progress notice

**Sentinel errors (fail-closed):**
- `V1DivergedError` — local v1 has commits not on remote (refuses to rebase)
- `BootstrapTooLargeError` — first push with too many unpushed commits (configurable via `ENTIRE_OPF_BOOTSTRAP_LIMIT`)
- `V1RefMovedError` — another worktree advanced the ref mid-rewrite (CAS conflict)
- `OPFRuntimeFailedError` — OPF binary failed mid-rewrite; push aborts before tagging anything

**Shadow-branch cleanup:**
- After successful push, vestigial shadow branches (ended sessions, no pending turn checkpoints) are auto-deleted
- Conservative safety predicate: active sessions or pending finalize protect their shadow

**Privacy contract:**
- Short-return from the OPF runtime trips the circuit breaker + aborts the rewrite (defense against silent under-redaction)
- Fail-closed everywhere: any runtime failure aborts the push rather than tagging 7-layer content as 8-layer-applied

## Why this shape

OPF inference is ~6s of CPU model-load per call. Earlier iterations ran OPF at commit time, which meant every commit in an agent loop paid that cost — terrible UX for sessions that produce 10+ commits before pushing. Moving OPF to pre-push aligns the cost with the user-visible "content leaves the machine" moment: one prompt per push, one wait, opt-out per push via env var.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run check` (fmt + lint + test:ci + Vogon canary + roger-roger external-agent canary) — green
- [x] Real-agent smoke test on a fresh repo with `private_person` + `private_email` enabled
- [x] End-to-end pre-push rewrite verified against a real `opf` binary
- [x] All four sentinel error paths exercised by integration tests
- [x] Fail-closed contract tests:
  - Short-return runtime trips breaker + aborts
  - Mid-rewrite runtime failure aborts before CAS
  - Diverged remote refuses to proceed
  - Bootstrap cap respects `ENTIRE_OPF_BOOTSTRAP_LIMIT`
- [x] Privacy contract tests:
  - `.md` and no-extension blobs inside a shard get redacted (slip-through prevention)
  - Idempotent re-run preserves trailer + tree

content.text: This is a large, security-sensitive PR (a privacy/redaction filter with fail-closed semantics, CAS concurrency, and pre-push rewrite logic). I'll read the core files myself and fan out focused reviewers in parallel over the independent subsystems, then synthesize.

input.prompt:
Review the OPF (OpenAI Privacy Filter) pre-push rewrite implementation on the current git branch `feat/openai-privacy-filter` (PR #1214). This is the security-critical core.

Focus on these files (read them in full):
- cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go (THE crux — pre-push re-redaction of unpushed entire/checkpoints/v1 commits, CAS ref update, sentinel errors)
- cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go
- cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_prompt.go
- cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go (the pre-push hook wiring)

Also skim cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite_test.go and manual_commit_opf_prompt_test.go to understand intended behavior.

The design contract (from CLAUDE.md and the PR body):
- OPF runs only at pre-push, never post-commit. Per-commit condensation stays on the fast 7-layer regex pipeline.
- Pre-push walks unpushed v1 commits, runs OPF over their blobs, rebuilds commits with `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` trailer, and atomically CAS-updates the local v1 ref before pushing.
- FAIL-CLOSED everywhere: any runtime failure must ABORT the push rather than tag 7-layer content as 8-layer-applied. A short-return from the OPF runtime must trip the circuit breaker and abort.
- Idempotent re-parenting: commits already tagged `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` are not re-redacted on retry.
- Shard scoping: only redact files inside the commit's own shard (`<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/*`); files outside the shard are byte-copied.
- Fail-closed extension policy: every regular file inside the shard (except `content_hash.txt`) flows through redaction.
- Sentinel errors (errors.As): V1DivergedError, BootstrapTooLargeError, V1RefMovedError, OPFRuntimeFailedError.

Scrutinize HARD for:
1. Any path where 7-layer-only content could be pushed but tagged as OPF-applied (the worst possible bug — silent under-redaction).
2. CAS / TOCTOU races on the v1 ref update (V1RefMovedError handling, multi-worktree concurrency).
3. Idempotency correctness: could re-running double-redact or skip redaction incorrectly? Trailer detection robustness.
4. Shard-scoping correctness: could a file that needs redaction be byte-copied because shard detection is wrong? Off-by-one on `id[:2]`/`id[2:]`.
5. Circuit-breaker / short-return detection: is "short return" detection sound, or can under-redaction slip through?
6. Error wrapping so errors.As works for the sentinels; partial-failure / abort-before-tagging ordering.
7. Divergence detection correctness (V1DivergedError) — could it false-negative and rebase over remote commits?

Report findings as a prioritized list (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Nit) with file:line references and concrete reasoning. Do NOT fix anything — review only. Be concrete and skeptical; quote the code. Return only your findings list, not file dumps.

input.prompt:
Review the OPF runtime shellout and redaction-pipeline integration on git branch `feat/openai-privacy-filter` (PR #1214).

Read in full:
- redact/opf.go (the `opf` binary shellout via `opfRuntime` interface, batched stdin joined with \x1e (record separator), JSON-aware leaf extraction, category mapping, circuit breaker)
- redact/redact.go (how OPF integrates as the 8th layer alongside the 7 always-on regex layers; the diff added ~168 lines)
- redact/testhelpers.go
Skim redact/opf_test.go and redact/redact_test.go to understand intended behavior.

Design contract:
- `opf` is a 1.5B token-classification model invoked as a subprocess. ~6s CPU model-load per call, so batching matters: one shellout per blob, all prose-shaped leaves joined with \x1e.
- Eight categories: private_person, private_email, private_phone, private_address, private_url, private_date, account_number, secret.
- Process-scoped circuit breaker: first runtime failure disables OPF for the rest of the invocation.
- JSON-aware: extract string leaves from JSON blobs, redact each, reassemble.
- FAIL-CLOSED: a short-return (fewer outputs than inputs) from the runtime must trip the breaker. Any runtime error must propagate so the caller aborts the push.

Scrutinize HARD for:
1. The \x1e batching protocol: what if a leaf VALUE itself contains \x1e or a newline? Could splitting the runtime output misalign inputs↔outputs and corrupt/mis-redact data? Injection or desync risk.
2. Offset/index mapping when re-inserting redacted leaves back into JSON — could redacted text land in the wrong field?
3. Short-return / count-mismatch detection: is it actually checked, and does it fail closed?
4. Subprocess handling: timeout enforcement, stdin/stdout deadlock (writing large stdin while child writes stdout — classic pipe-buffer deadlock), context cancellation, stderr capture, exit-code handling, zombie processes.
5. Category mapping correctness: are model output labels mapped to the right redaction replacement? Any category that silently no-ops?
6. Encoding issues: non-UTF8 bytes in blobs, very large blobs, empty leaves.
7. Circuit breaker thread-safety if invoked concurrently.

Report findings as a prioritized list (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Nit) with file:line references and concrete reasoning, quoting code. Do NOT fix — review only. Return only the findings list.

124		var o condenseOpts
125		if len(opts) > 0 {
126			o = opts[0]
127		}
128		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
129		condenseStart := time.Now()
130	
131		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
132		ref, hasShadowBranch := resolveShadowRef(repo, shadowBranchName, o.shadowRef)
133	
134		// Re-resolve transcript path before any reads — handles agents that relocate
135		// transcripts mid-session (e.g., Cursor CLI flat → nested layout change).
136		// Errors are ignored; downstream readers handle missing transcripts gracefully.
137		resolveTranscriptPath(state) //nolint:errcheck,gosec // best-effort; downstream readers handle missing files
138	
139		extractStart := time.Now()
140		_, extractSessionDataSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "extract_session_data")
141		var shadowHash plumbing.Hash
142		if hasShadowBranch {
143			shadowHash = ref.Hash()
144		}
145		sessionData, extractErr := s.extractOrCreateSessionData(ctx, repo, ag, shadowHash, hasShadowBranch, state)
146		if extractErr != nil {
147			extractSessionDataSpan.RecordError(extractErr)
148			extractSessionDataSpan.End()
149			return nil, extractErr
150		}
151		extractSessionDataSpan.End()
152		extractDuration := time.Since(extractStart)
153	
154		// Backfill session state token usage from the freshly-extracted transcript.
155		// Copilot CLI writes session.shutdown after the hooks return, so by condensation
156		// time we can recover the authoritative full-session total from the transcript
157		// while keeping checkpoint metadata scoped to CheckpointTranscriptStart.
158		if backfillUsage := sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage(ctx, ag, state.AgentType, sessionData.Transcript, sessionData.TokenUsage); backfillUsage != nil {
159			state.TokenUsage = backfillUsage
160		}
161	
162		// Backfill the model from the transcript for agents that don't report it via
163		// hooks (e.g., Pi records message.model but its hook events carry no model
164		// field). Only fills when the model is otherwise unknown — hook-reported
165		// models take precedence.
166		if state.ModelName == "" {
167			if model := sessionStateBackfillModel(ctx, ag, sessionData.Transcript); model != "" {
168				state.ModelName = model
169			}
170		}
171	
172		// Skip gate: if there is no transcript AND no files touched, there is nothing
173		// meaningful to condense. Return early to avoid writing metadata-only stubs.
174		//
175		// This check MUST run before filterFilesTouched. That function's fallback
176		// assigns all committed files to sessions with empty FilesTouched (designed
177		// for mid-turn commits where SaveStep hasn't run yet). Without this ordering,
178		// genuinely empty sessions (no transcript, no shadow branch, no tracked files)
179		// would acquire committed files from the fallback and bypass this gate.
180		if len(sessionData.Transcript) == 0 && len(sessionData.FilesTouched) == 0 {
181			logging.Info(logCtx, "session skipped: no transcript or files to condense",
182				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
183				slog.String("agent_type", string(state.AgentType)),
184				slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
185				slog.Bool("has_shadow_branch", hasShadowBranch),
186				slog.String("transcript_path", state.TranscriptPath),
187			)
188			return newSkippedResult(checkpointID, state.SessionID), nil
189		}
190	
191		filterFilesTouched(sessionData, committedFiles, state)
192	
193		redactedTranscript, redactDuration := redactOrDrop(logCtx, sessionData.Transcript, state.SessionID, checkpointID)
194		if skipped := skipIfPostRedactionEmpty(logCtx, redactedTranscript, sessionData, state, checkpointID); skipped != nil {
195			return skipped, nil
196		}
197	
198		store := s.getCheckpointStore(repo)
199	
200		// Get author info
201		authorName, authorEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(repo)
202	
203		// Determine attribution base commit
204		attrBase := state.AttributionBaseCommit
205		if attrBase == "" {
206			attrBase = state.BaseCommit
207		}
208	
209		attributionStart := time.Now()
210		attrCtx, attributionSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "calculate_session_attribution")
211		attribution := calculateSessionAttributions(attrCtx, repo, ref, sessionData, state, attributionOpts{
212			headTree:              o.headTree,
213			parentTree:            o.parentTree,
214			repoDir:               o.repoDir,
215			attributionBaseCommit: attrBase,
216			parentCommitHash:      o.parentCommitHash,
217			headCommitHash:        o.headCommitHash,
218			allAgentFiles:         o.allAgentFiles,
219		})
220		attributionSpan.End()
221		attributionDuration := time.Since(attributionStart)
222	
223		// Get current branch name
224		branchName := GetCurrentBranchName(repo)
225	
226		var summary *cpkg.Summary
227		if settings.IsSummarizeEnabled(ctx) && redactedTranscript.Len() > 0 {
228			summary = generateSummary(ctx, redactedTranscript, sessionData.FilesTouched, state)
229		}
230	
231		// Post-commit emits 7-layer-only blobs. OPF runs later in the
232		// pre-push rewrite path, never here.
233		skillEvents := mergeSkillEvents(state.SkillEvents, withSkillEventTurnID(sessionData.SkillEvents, state.TurnID))
234	
235		writeOpts := cpkg.WriteCommittedOptions{
236			CheckpointID:                checkpointID,
237			SessionID:                   state.SessionID,
238			Strategy:                    StrategyNameManualCommit,
239			Branch:                      branchName,
240			Transcript:                  redactedTranscript,
241			Prompts:                     sessionData.Prompts,
242			FilesTouched:                sessionData.FilesTouched,
243			CheckpointsCount:            state.StepCount,
244			EphemeralBranch:             shadowBranchName,
245			AuthorName:                  authorName,
246			AuthorEmail:                 authorEmail,
247			Agent:                       state.AgentType,
248			Model:                       state.ModelName,
249			TurnID:                      state.TurnID,
250			TranscriptIdentifierAtStart: state.TranscriptIdentifierAtStart,
251			CheckpointTranscriptStart:   state.CheckpointTranscriptStart,
252			TokenUsage:                  sessionData.TokenUsage,
253			SkillEvents:                 skillEvents,
254			SessionMetrics:              buildSessionMetrics(state),
255			InitialAttribution:          attribution,
256			PromptAttributionsJSON:      marshalPromptAttributionsIncludingPending(state),
257			Summary:                     summary,
258			Kind:                        string(state.Kind),
259			ReviewSkills:                state.ReviewSkills,
260			ReviewPrompt:                state.ReviewPrompt,
261			HasReview:                   state.Kind.IsReview(),
262			HasInvestigation:            state.Kind.IsInvestigate(),
263			InvestigateRunID:            state.InvestigateRunID,
264			InvestigateTopic:            state.InvestigateTopic,
265		}
266	
267		writeV1Start := time.Now()
268		writeCtx, writeCommittedSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "write_committed_v1")
269		if err := store.WriteCommitted(writeCtx, writeOpts); err != nil {
270			writeCommittedSpan.RecordError(err)
271			writeCommittedSpan.End()
272			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write checkpoint metadata: %w", err)
273		}
274		writeCommittedSpan.End()
275		writeV1Duration := time.Since(writeV1Start)
276	
277		// Mirror the committed write to the v1 custom ref when opted in
278		// (local-only, never pushed; failures are logged, not fatal).
279		MirrorCommittedMetadataRefBestEffort(ctx, repo)
280	
281		logging.Debug(logCtx, "condense timings",
282			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
283			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
284			slog.Int64("extract_session_data_ms", extractDuration.Milliseconds()),
285			slog.Int64("calculate_session_attribution_ms", attributionDuration.Milliseconds()),
286			slog.Int64("redact_transcript_ms", redactDuration.Milliseconds()),
287			slog.Int64("write_committed_v1_ms", writeV1Duration.Milliseconds()),
288			slog.Int64("total_ms", time.Since(condenseStart).Milliseconds()),
289			slog.Int("transcript_bytes", len(sessionData.Transcript)),
290			slog.Int("transcript_lines", sessionData.FullTranscriptLines),
291		)
292	
293		return &CondenseResult{
294			CheckpointID:         checkpointID,
295			SessionID:            state.SessionID,
296			CheckpointsCount:     state.StepCount,
297			FilesTouched:         sessionData.FilesTouched,
298			Prompts:              sessionData.Prompts,
299			TotalTranscriptLines: sessionData.FullTranscriptLines,
300			Transcript:           sessionData.Transcript,
301		}, nil
302	}

304	// redactOrDrop runs redactSessionTranscript and, on failure, logs a warning
305	// and returns empty bytes. Drop-on-failure is the long-standing contract here:
306	// hooks have no retry path, and a failed redaction must not block the commit.
307	func redactOrDrop(logCtx context.Context, transcript []byte, sessionID string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (redact.RedactedBytes, time.Duration) {
308		redactedTranscript, redactDuration, err := redactSessionTranscript(logCtx, transcript)
309		if err != nil {
310			logging.Warn(logCtx, "failed to redact transcript secrets, dropping transcript for checkpoint",
311				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
312				slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
313				slog.String("error", err.Error()),
314			)
315			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, redactDuration
316		}
317		return redactedTranscript, redactDuration
318	}

320	// skipIfPostRedactionEmpty returns a Skipped result when redaction emptied the
321	// transcript AND the filtered FilesTouched is also empty. Without this, a
322	// session that passed the pre-redaction gate but got its transcript dropped by
323	// a malformed-JSONL redaction error would write a metadata-only stub.
324	func skipIfPostRedactionEmpty(logCtx context.Context, redactedTranscript redact.RedactedBytes, sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, state *SessionState, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) *CondenseResult {
325		if redactedTranscript.Len() > 0 || len(sessionData.FilesTouched) > 0 {
326			return nil
327		}
328		logging.Info(logCtx, "session skipped: nothing to persist after redaction",
329			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
330			slog.String("agent_type", string(state.AgentType)),
331			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
332		)
333		return newSkippedResult(checkpointID, state.SessionID)
334	}

336	func newSkippedResult(checkpointID id.CheckpointID, sessionID string) *CondenseResult {
337		return &CondenseResult{
338			CheckpointID: checkpointID,
339			SessionID:    sessionID,
340			Skipped:      true,
341		}
342	}

344	// redactSessionTranscript redacts the transcript once for use by both the compact
345	// package and the checkpoint stores. Returns the redacted bytes and the duration
346	// of the redaction operation for perf logging.
347	func redactSessionTranscript(ctx context.Context, transcript []byte) (redact.RedactedBytes, time.Duration, error) {
348		start := time.Now()
349		_, span := perf.Start(ctx, "redact_transcript")
350		defer span.End()
351	
352		if len(transcript) == 0 {
353			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, time.Since(start), nil
354		}
355	
356		redacted, err := redactSessionJSONLBytes(ctx, transcript)
357		if err != nil {
358			span.RecordError(err)
359			return redact.RedactedBytes{}, time.Since(start), fmt.Errorf("failed to redact transcript secrets: %w", err)
360		}
361		return redacted, time.Since(start), nil
362	}

364	// resolveShadowRef returns the shadow branch reference, preferring a pre-resolved
365	// ref when available and falling back to a repo lookup.
366	func resolveShadowRef(repo *git.Repository, branchName string, preResolved *plumbing.Reference) (ref *plumbing.Reference, exists bool) {
367		if preResolved != nil {
368			return preResolved, true
369		}
370		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName)
371		resolved, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
372		if err != nil {
373			return nil, false
374		}
375		return resolved, true
376	}

378	// filterFilesTouched narrows sessionData.FilesTouched to files present in
379	// committedFiles. When no prior files were recorded, it falls back to the
380	// committed set (minus Entire metadata) — but only when sessionHasEvidenceOfWork
381	// is true. The fallback was originally unconditional, which let sessions that
382	// were registered at SessionStart but never produced anything (e.g. ephemeral
383	// Codex sessions whose hooks fired with a null transcript_path and never
384	// reached SaveStep) inherit another session's committed files.
385	func filterFilesTouched(sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, committedFiles map[string]struct{}, state *SessionState) {
386		if len(committedFiles) == 0 {
387			return
388		}
389		if len(sessionData.FilesTouched) > 0 {
390			filtered := make([]string, 0, len(sessionData.FilesTouched))
391			for _, f := range sessionData.FilesTouched {
392				if _, ok := committedFiles[f]; ok {
393					filtered = append(filtered, f)
394				}
395			}
396			sessionData.FilesTouched = filtered
397			return
398		}
399		if !sessionHasEvidenceOfWork(sessionData, state) {
400			return
401		}
402		sessionData.FilesTouched = committedFilesExcludingMetadata(committedFiles)
403	}
404	
405	// sessionHasEvidenceOfWork returns true when the session looks like a real
406	// participant — either it produced a readable transcript or a prior SaveStep
407	// recorded a checkpoint (StepCount > 0). False means the session was likely
408	// registered but never did anything; treating such a session as the author of
409	// the committed files would attribute another session's work to it.
410	func sessionHasEvidenceOfWork(sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, state *SessionState) bool {
411		if len(sessionData.Transcript) > 0 {
412			return true
413		}
414		return state != nil && state.StepCount > 0
415	}

417	// extractOrCreateSessionData tries to extract session data from the shadow branch,
418	// live transcript, or creates empty session data as a fallback. The empty case is
419	// handled by the skip gate in CondenseSession.
420	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) extractOrCreateSessionData(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, ag agent.Agent, shadowHash plumbing.Hash, hasShadowBranch bool, state *SessionState) (*ExtractedSessionData, error) {
421		switch {
422		case hasShadowBranch:
423			// Shadow branch exists (from SaveStep commits) — extract transcript and
424			// metadata from the branch tree, preferring the live transcript if fresher.
425			data, err := s.extractSessionData(ctx, repo, shadowHash, state.SessionID, state.FilesTouched, state.AgentType, state.TranscriptPath, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart, state.Phase.IsActive())
426			if err != nil {
427				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to extract session data: %w", err)
428			}
429			return data, nil
430		case state.TranscriptPath != "":
431			// No shadow branch but a live transcript path is known — read directly
432			// from disk. This handles mid-session commits before SaveStep runs.
433			if state.Phase.IsActive() {
434				prepareTranscriptIfNeeded(ctx, ag, state.TranscriptPath)
435			}
436			data, err := s.extractSessionDataFromLiveTranscript(ctx, state)
437			if err != nil {
438				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to extract session data from live transcript: %w", err)
439			}
440			return data, nil
441		default:
442			// No shadow branch and no transcript path — create empty session data.
443			// This happens for sessions where the agent never set TranscriptPath
444			// (e.g., Codex hooks may send null transcript_path). The skip gate in
445			// CondenseSession will skip condensation if nothing is found.
446			logging.Debug(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint"),
447				"no shadow branch and no transcript path, returning empty session data",
448				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
449				slog.String("agent_type", string(state.AgentType)),
450			)
451			return &ExtractedSessionData{
452				FilesTouched: state.FilesTouched,
453			}, nil
454		}
455	}

457	// generateSummary produces an LLM-generated summary of the session transcript.
458	// The transcript must be pre-redacted to avoid sending secrets to the LLM.
459	// Returns nil if the scoped transcript is empty or generation fails.
460	func generateSummary(ctx context.Context, redactedTranscript redact.RedactedBytes, filesTouched []string, state *SessionState) *cpkg.Summary {
461		summarizeCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "summarize")
462		transcriptBytes := redactedTranscript.Bytes()
463	
464		var scopedTranscript []byte
465		switch state.AgentType {
466		case agent.AgentTypeGemini:
467			scoped, sliceErr := geminicli.SliceFromMessage(transcriptBytes, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
468			if sliceErr != nil {
469				logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "failed to scope Gemini transcript for summary",
470					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
471					slog.String("error", sliceErr.Error()))
472			}
473			scopedTranscript = scoped
474		case agent.AgentTypeOpenCode:
475			scoped, sliceErr := opencode.SliceFromMessage(transcriptBytes, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
476			if sliceErr != nil {
477				logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "failed to scope OpenCode transcript for summary",
478					slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
479					slog.String("error", sliceErr.Error()))
480			}
481			scopedTranscript = scoped
482		case agent.AgentTypeCodex, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, agent.AgentTypeCursor, agent.AgentTypeFactoryAIDroid, agent.AgentTypeUnknown:
483			scopedTranscript = transcript.SliceFromLine(transcriptBytes, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
484		}
485	
486		if len(scopedTranscript) == 0 {
487			return nil
488		}
489	
490		generator := buildSummaryGenerator(summarizeCtx)
491		// scopedTranscript is sliced from redactedTranscript, which was redacted earlier in CondenseSession.
492		summary, err := summarize.GenerateFromTranscript(summarizeCtx, redact.AlreadyRedacted(scopedTranscript), filesTouched, state.AgentType, generator)
493		if err != nil {
494			logging.Warn(summarizeCtx, "summary generation failed",
495				slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
496				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
497			return nil
498		}
499		logging.Info(summarizeCtx, "summary generated",
500			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID))
501		return summary
502	}
503	
504	// buildSummaryGenerator returns a Generator based on the configured summary provider.
505	// Returns nil if no provider is configured (GenerateFromTranscript falls back to ClaudeGenerator).
506	//
507	// The return type is the summarize.Generator interface rather than the concrete
508	// adapter pointer so callers can't accidentally hold a non-nil interface that
509	// wraps a nil pointer (the classic Go nil-interface footgun).
510	func buildSummaryGenerator(ctx context.Context) summarize.Generator { //nolint:ireturn,nolintlint // interface return is intentional for provider abstraction and nil-safety; nolintlint flagged as "unused" under some linter versions but ireturn fires in others
511		s, err := settings.Load(ctx)
512		if err != nil {
513			// Warn (not Debug): this is the auto-summarize hot path on every commit.
514			// A settings-load failure silently downgrades the user's configured
515			// provider to the default, and Debug would hide that from operators.
516			logging.Warn(ctx, "could not load settings for summary provider, using default",
517				"error", err.Error())
518			return nil
519		}
520		if s.SummaryGeneration == nil || s.SummaryGeneration.Provider == "" {
521			return nil
522		}
523	
524		providerName := types.AgentName(s.SummaryGeneration.Provider)
525		ag, err := agent.Get(providerName)
526		if err != nil {
527			discoverExternalSummaryProviders(ctx)
528			ag, err = agent.Get(providerName)
529			if err != nil {
530				logging.Warn(ctx, "configured summary provider not available, using default",
531					"provider", s.SummaryGeneration.Provider, "error", err.Error())
532				return nil
533			}
534		}
535	
536		tg, ok := agent.AsTextGenerator(ag)
537		if !ok {
538			logging.Warn(ctx, "configured summary provider does not support text generation, using default",
539				"provider", s.SummaryGeneration.Provider)
540			return nil
541		}
542	
543		// Check binary on PATH, not DetectPresence — a repo can use one agent
544		// for development while a different agent generates summaries. Fall back
545		// silently (Warn log) because this runs in the post-commit hook and a
546		// hard error would block the commit.
547		if !external.IsExternal(ag) && !isSummaryProviderCLIAvailable(providerName) {
548			logging.Warn(ctx, "configured summary provider CLI binary not on PATH, using default",
549				"provider", s.SummaryGeneration.Provider)
550			return nil
551		}
552	
553		return &summarize.TextGeneratorAdapter{
554			TextGenerator: tg,
555			Model:         summarize.ResolveModel(providerName, s.SummaryGeneration.Model),
556		}
557	}

559	// marshalPromptAttributionsIncludingPending builds the complete prompt attribution slice
560	// (including PendingPromptAttribution for mid-turn commits) and encodes it to JSON.
561	// This must stay consistent with the slice used by calculateSessionAttributions so the
562	// persisted diagnostics match the computed InitialAttribution.
563	func marshalPromptAttributionsIncludingPending(state *SessionState) json.RawMessage {
564		pas := make([]PromptAttribution, len(state.PromptAttributions), len(state.PromptAttributions)+1)
565		copy(pas, state.PromptAttributions)
566		if state.PendingPromptAttribution != nil {
567			pas = append(pas, *state.PendingPromptAttribution)
568		}
569		if len(pas) == 0 {
570			return nil
571		}
572		data, err := json.Marshal(pas)
573		if err != nil {
574			return nil
575		}
576		return data
577	}

593	func hasTokenUsageData(usage *agent.TokenUsage) bool {
594		if usage == nil {
595			return false
596		}
597	
598		if usage.InputTokens > 0 || usage.CacheCreationTokens > 0 || usage.CacheReadTokens > 0 || usage.OutputTokens > 0 || usage.APICallCount > 0 {
599			return true
600		}
601	
602		return hasTokenUsageData(usage.SubagentTokens)
603	}

605	// sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage returns the best session-level token usage to
606	// persist in session state after condensation.
607	func sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, agentType types.AgentType, transcript []byte, checkpointUsage *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
608		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeCopilotCLI && len(transcript) > 0 {
609			fullSessionUsage := agent.CalculateTokenUsage(ctx, ag, transcript, 0, "")
610			if hasTokenUsageData(fullSessionUsage) {
611				return fullSessionUsage
612			}
613			logging.Debug(ctx, "copilot-cli: full-session token read produced no data, falling back to checkpoint usage")
614		}
615	
616		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeCopilotCLI && hasTokenUsageData(checkpointUsage) {
617			return checkpointUsage
618		}
619	
620		if checkpointUsage != nil && checkpointUsage.InputTokens > 0 {
621			return checkpointUsage
622		}
623	
624		return nil
625	}

627	// sessionStateBackfillModel extracts the LLM model from the transcript for
628	// agents that don't report it through hooks (e.g., Pi). Returns "" when the
629	// agent doesn't support model extraction, the transcript is empty, or no model
630	// can be determined. Errors are debug-logged because callers treat "" as "no
631	// model available".
632	func sessionStateBackfillModel(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, transcript []byte) string {
633		me, ok := agent.AsModelExtractor(ag)
634		if !ok {
635			return ""
636		}
637		model, err := me.ExtractModel(transcript)
638		if err != nil {
639			logging.Debug(ctx, "model backfill from transcript failed", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
640			return ""
641		}
642		return model
643	}

645	// attributionOpts provides pre-resolved git objects to avoid redundant reads.
646	type attributionOpts struct {
647		headTree              *object.Tree        // HEAD commit tree (already resolved by PostCommit)
648		shadowTree            *object.Tree        // Shadow branch tree (already resolved by PostCommit)
649		parentTree            *object.Tree        // Parent commit tree (nil for initial commits, for consistent non-agent line counting)
650		repoDir               string              // Repository worktree path for git CLI commands
651		parentCommitHash      string              // HEAD's first parent hash (preferred diff base for non-agent files)
652		attributionBaseCommit string              // Base commit hash for non-agent file detection (empty = fall back to go-git tree walk)
653		headCommitHash        string              // HEAD commit hash for non-agent file detection (empty = fall back to go-git tree walk)
654		allAgentFiles         map[string]struct{} // Union of all sessions' FilesTouched (nil = single-session)

657	func calculateSessionAttributions(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, shadowRef *plumbing.Reference, sessionData *ExtractedSessionData, state *SessionState, opts ...attributionOpts) *cpkg.InitialAttribution {
658		// Calculate initial attribution using accumulated prompt attribution data.
659		// This uses user edits captured at each prompt start (before agent works),
660		// plus any user edits after the final checkpoint (shadow → head).
661		//
662		// When shadowRef is nil (agent committed mid-turn before SaveStep),
663		// HEAD is used as the shadow tree. This is correct because the agent's
664		// commit IS HEAD — there are no user edits between agent work and commit.
665		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "attribution")
666	
667		var o attributionOpts
668		if len(opts) > 0 {
669			o = opts[0]
670		}
671	
672		headTree := o.headTree
673		if headTree == nil {
674			headRef, headErr := repo.Head()
675			if headErr != nil {
676				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD",
677					slog.String("error", headErr.Error()))
678				return nil
679			}
680	
681			headCommit, commitErr := repo.CommitObject(headRef.Hash())
682			if commitErr != nil {
683				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD commit",
684					slog.String("error", commitErr.Error()))
685				return nil
686			}
687	
688			var treeErr error
689			headTree, treeErr = headCommit.Tree()
690			if treeErr != nil {
691				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get HEAD tree",
692					slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
693				return nil
694			}
695		}
696	
697		// Get shadow tree: from pre-resolved cache, shadow branch, or HEAD (agent committed directly).
698		shadowTree := o.shadowTree
699		if shadowTree == nil {
700			if shadowRef != nil {
701				shadowCommit, shadowErr := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef.Hash())
702				if shadowErr != nil {
703					logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow commit",
704						slog.String("error", shadowErr.Error()),
705						slog.String("shadow_ref", shadowRef.Hash().String()))
706					return nil
707				}
708				var shadowTreeErr error
709				shadowTree, shadowTreeErr = shadowCommit.Tree()
710				if shadowTreeErr != nil {
711					logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution skipped: failed to get shadow tree",
712						slog.String("error", shadowTreeErr.Error()))
713					return nil
714				}
715			} else {
716				// No shadow branch: agent committed mid-turn. Use HEAD as shadow
717				// because the agent's work is the commit itself.
718				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: using HEAD as shadow (no shadow branch)")
719				shadowTree = headTree
720			}
721		}
722	
723		// Get base tree (state before session started)
724		var baseTree *object.Tree
725		attrBase := state.AttributionBaseCommit
726		if attrBase == "" {
727			attrBase = state.BaseCommit // backward compat
728		}
729		if baseCommit, baseErr := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(attrBase)); baseErr == nil {
730			if tree, baseTErr := baseCommit.Tree(); baseTErr == nil {
731				baseTree = tree
732			} else {
733				logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base tree unavailable",
734					slog.String("error", baseTErr.Error()))
735			}
736		} else {
737			logging.Debug(logCtx, "attribution: base commit unavailable",
738				slog.String("error", baseErr.Error()),
739				slog.String("attribution_base", attrBase))
740		}
741	
742		// Include PendingPromptAttribution if it was never moved to PromptAttributions.
743		// This happens when an agent commits mid-turn without calling SaveStep (e.g., Codex).
744		// PendingPromptAttribution is set during UserPromptSubmit but only moved to
745		// PromptAttributions during SaveStep. Without this, mid-turn commits have no PA
746		// data and pre-session worktree dirt cannot be identified for baseline exclusion.
747		promptAttrs := state.PromptAttributions
748		if state.PendingPromptAttribution != nil {
749			promptAttrs = append(promptAttrs, *state.PendingPromptAttribution)
750		}
751	
752		// Log accumulated prompt attributions for debugging
753		var totalUserAdded, totalUserRemoved int
754		for i, pa := range promptAttrs {
755			totalUserAdded += pa.UserLinesAdded
756			totalUserRemoved += pa.UserLinesRemoved
757			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution data",
758				slog.Int("checkpoint", pa.CheckpointNumber),
759				slog.Int("user_added", pa.UserLinesAdded),
760				slog.Int("user_removed", pa.UserLinesRemoved),
761				slog.Int("agent_added", pa.AgentLinesAdded),
762				slog.Int("agent_removed", pa.AgentLinesRemoved),
763				slog.Int("index", i))
764		}
765	
766		attribution := CalculateAttributionWithAccumulated(ctx, AttributionParams{
767			BaseTree:              baseTree,
768			ShadowTree:            shadowTree,
769			HeadTree:              headTree,
770			ParentTree:            o.parentTree,
771			FilesTouched:          sessionData.FilesTouched,
772			PromptAttributions:    promptAttrs,
773			RepoDir:               o.repoDir,
774			ParentCommitHash:      o.parentCommitHash,
775			AttributionBaseCommit: attrBase,
776			HeadCommitHash:        o.headCommitHash,
777			AllAgentFiles:         o.allAgentFiles,
778		})
779	
780		if attribution != nil {
781			logging.Info(logCtx, "attribution calculated",
782				slog.Int("agent_lines", attribution.AgentLines),
783				slog.Int("human_added", attribution.HumanAdded),
784				slog.Int("human_modified", attribution.HumanModified),
785				slog.Int("human_removed", attribution.HumanRemoved),
786				slog.Int("total_committed", attribution.TotalCommitted),
787				slog.Float64("agent_percentage", attribution.AgentPercentage),
788				slog.Int("accumulated_user_added", totalUserAdded),
789				slog.Int("accumulated_user_removed", totalUserRemoved),
790				slog.Int("files_touched", len(sessionData.FilesTouched)))
791		}
792	
793		return attribution
794	}

796	// committedFilesExcludingMetadata returns committed files with CLI- and
797	// agent-managed paths filtered out. Files under `.entire/`, `.git/`, agent
798	// config directories (e.g. `.cursor/`, `.claude/`), and registered protected
799	// files (e.g. `opencode.json`) are created by `entire enable` or the agent
800	// integration itself, not by user-prompted work, so they should not appear in
801	// files_touched when this fallback fires for sessions with no FilesTouched.
802	func committedFilesExcludingMetadata(committedFiles map[string]struct{}) []string {
803		protectedFiles := agent.AllProtectedFiles()
804		result := make([]string, 0, len(committedFiles))
805		for f := range committedFiles {
806			if isProtectedPath(f) {
807				continue
808			}
809			if slices.Contains(protectedFiles, f) {
810				continue
811			}
812			result = append(result, f)
813		}
814		slices.Sort(result)
815		return result
816	}

818	// extractSessionData extracts session data from the shadow branch.
819	// filesTouched is the list of files tracked during the session (from SessionState.FilesTouched).
820	// agentType identifies the agent (e.g., "Gemini CLI", "Claude Code") to determine transcript format.
821	// liveTranscriptPath, when non-empty and readable, is preferred over the shadow branch copy.
822	// This handles the case where SaveStep was skipped (no code changes) but the transcript
823	// continued growing — the shadow branch copy would be stale.
824	// checkpointTranscriptStart is the line offset (Claude) or message index (Gemini) where the current checkpoint began.
825	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) extractSessionData(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, shadowRef plumbing.Hash, sessionID string, filesTouched []string, agentType types.AgentType, liveTranscriptPath string, checkpointTranscriptStart int, isActive bool) (*ExtractedSessionData, error) {
826		ag, _ := agent.GetByAgentType(agentType) //nolint:errcheck // ag may be nil for unknown agent types; callers use type assertions so nil is safe
827		commit, err := repo.CommitObject(shadowRef)
828		if err != nil {
829			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
830		}
831	
832		tree, err := commit.Tree()
833		if err != nil {
834			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
835		}
836	
837		data := &ExtractedSessionData{}
838		// sessionID is already an "entire session ID" (with date prefix)
839		metadataDir := paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)
840	
841		// Extract transcript — prefer the live file when available, fall back to shadow branch.
842		// The shadow branch copy may be stale if the last turn ended without code changes
843		// (SaveStep is only called when there are file modifications).
844		var fullTranscript string
845		if liveTranscriptPath != "" {
846			// Ensure transcript file exists (OpenCode creates it lazily via `opencode export`).
847			// Only wait for flush when the session is active — for idle/ended sessions the
848			// transcript is already fully flushed (the Stop hook completed the flush).
849			if isActive {
850				prepareTranscriptIfNeeded(ctx, ag, liveTranscriptPath)
851			}
852			if liveData, readErr := os.ReadFile(liveTranscriptPath); readErr == nil && len(liveData) > 0 { //nolint:gosec // path from session state
853				fullTranscript = string(liveData)
854			}
855		}
856		if fullTranscript == "" {
857			// Fall back to shadow branch copy
858			if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
859				if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
860					fullTranscript = content
861				}
862			} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
863				if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
864					fullTranscript = content
865				}
866			}
867		}
868	
869		// Process transcript based on agent type
870		if fullTranscript != "" {
871			data.Transcript = []byte(fullTranscript)
872			data.FullTranscriptLines = countTranscriptItems(agentType, fullTranscript)
873			// Read prompts from shadow branch tree (source of truth after SaveStep)
874			if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.PromptFileName); fileErr == nil {
875				if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil && content != "" {
876					data.Prompts = splitPromptContent(content)
877				}
878			}
879			// Filesystem fallback (written at turn start, covers mid-turn commits)
880			if len(data.Prompts) == 0 {
881				data.Prompts = readPromptsFromFilesystem(ctx, sessionID)
882			}
883		}
884	
885		// Use tracked files from session state (not all files in tree)
886		data.FilesTouched = filesTouched
887	
888		// Calculate token usage from the checkpoint-scoped transcript portion.
889		// Skill events annotate the stored raw transcript, which is full-session, so
890		// extract them from offset 0; consumers can filter by checkpoint_transcript_start
891		// if they only render the checkpoint-scoped slice.
892		if len(data.Transcript) > 0 {
893			data.TokenUsage = agent.CalculateTokenUsage(ctx, ag, data.Transcript, checkpointTranscriptStart, "") //TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?
894			data.SkillEvents = agent.ExtractSkillEvents(ctx, ag, data.Transcript, 0)
895		}
896	
897		return data, nil
898	}

903		data := &ExtractedSessionData{}

942	// countTranscriptItems counts lines (JSONL) or messages (JSON) in a transcript.
943	// For Claude Code and JSONL-based agents, this counts lines.
944	// For Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and JSON-based agents, this counts messages.
945	// Returns 0 if the content is empty or malformed.
946	func countTranscriptItems(agentType types.AgentType, content string) int {
947		if content == "" {
948			return 0
949		}
950	
951		// OpenCode uses export JSON format with {"info": {...}, "messages": [...]}
952		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeOpenCode {
953			session, err := opencode.ParseExportSession([]byte(content))
954			if err == nil && session != nil {
955				return len(session.Messages)
956			}
957			return 0
958		}
959	
960		// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
961		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
962			transcript, err := geminicli.ParseTranscript([]byte(content))
963			if err == nil && transcript != nil && len(transcript.Messages) > 0 {
964				return len(transcript.Messages)
965			}
966			// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return 0
967			if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
968				return 0
969			}
970			// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
971		}
972	
973		// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
974		allLines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
975		// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
976		for len(allLines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(allLines[len(allLines)-1]) == "" {
977			allLines = allLines[:len(allLines)-1]
978		}
979		return len(allLines)
980	}

982	// extractUserPrompts extracts all user prompts from transcript content.
983	// Returns prompts with IDE context tags stripped (e.g., <ide_opened_file>).
984	func extractUserPrompts(agentType types.AgentType, content string) []string {
985		if content == "" {
986			return nil
987		}
988	
989		// Droid has its own envelope format — use its parser to normalize first
990		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeFactoryAIDroid {
991			lines, _, err := factoryaidroid.ParseDroidTranscriptFromBytes([]byte(content), 0)
992			if err != nil {
993				return nil
994			}
995			var prompts []string
996			for _, line := range lines {
997				if line.Type != transcript.TypeUser {
998					continue
999				}
1000				if text := transcript.ExtractUserContent(line.Message); text != "" {
1001					if stripped := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(text); stripped != "" {
1002						prompts = append(prompts, stripped)
1003					}
1004				}
1005			}
1006			return prompts
1007		}
1008	
1009		// OpenCode uses JSONL with a different per-line schema than Claude Code
1010		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeOpenCode {
1011			prompts, err := opencode.ExtractAllUserPrompts([]byte(content))
1012			if err == nil && len(prompts) > 0 {
1013				cleaned := make([]string, 0, len(prompts))
1014				for _, prompt := range prompts {
1015					if stripped := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(prompt); stripped != "" {
1016						cleaned = append(cleaned, stripped)
1017					}
1018				}
1019				return cleaned
1020			}
1021			return nil
1022		}
1023	
1024		// Try Gemini format first if agentType is Gemini, or as fallback if Unknown
1025		if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini || agentType == agent.AgentTypeUnknown {
1026			prompts, err := geminicli.ExtractAllUserPrompts([]byte(content))
1027			if err == nil && len(prompts) > 0 {
1028				// Strip IDE context tags for consistency with Claude Code handling
1029				cleaned := make([]string, 0, len(prompts))
1030				for _, prompt := range prompts {
1031					if stripped := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(prompt); stripped != "" {
1032						cleaned = append(cleaned, stripped)
1033					}
1034				}
1035				return cleaned
1036			}
1037			// If agentType is explicitly Gemini but parsing failed, return nil
1038			if agentType == agent.AgentTypeGemini {
1039				return nil
1040			}
1041			// Otherwise fall through to JSONL parsing for Unknown type
1042		}
1043	
1044		// Claude Code and other JSONL-based agents
1045		return extractUserPromptsFromLines(strings.Split(content, "\n"))
1046	}

1048	// extractUserPromptsFromLines extracts user prompts from JSONL transcript lines.
1049	// IDE-injected context tags (like <ide_opened_file>) are stripped from the results.
1050	func extractUserPromptsFromLines(lines []string) []string {
1051		var prompts []string
1052		for _, line := range lines {
1053			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
1054			if line == "" {
1055				continue
1056			}
1057	
1058			var entry map[string]interface{}
1059			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &entry); err != nil {
1060				continue
1061			}
1062	
1063			// Check for user message:
1064			// - Claude Code uses "type": "human" or "type": "user"
1065			// - Cursor uses "role": "user"
1066			msgType, _ := entry["type"].(string) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion on interface{} from JSON
1067			msgRole, _ := entry["role"].(string) //nolint:errcheck // type assertion on interface{} from JSON
1068			isUser := msgType == "human" || msgType == "user" || msgRole == "user"
1069			if !isUser {
1070				continue
1071			}
1072	
1073			// Extract message content
1074			message, ok := entry["message"].(map[string]interface{})
1075			if !ok {
1076				continue
1077			}
1078	
1079			// Handle string content
1080			if content, ok := message["content"].(string); ok && content != "" {
1081				cleaned := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(content)
1082				if cleaned != "" {
1083					prompts = append(prompts, cleaned)
1084				}
1085				continue
1086			}
1087	
1088			// Handle array content (e.g., multiple text blocks from VSCode)
1089			if arr, ok := message["content"].([]interface{}); ok {
1090				var texts []string
1091				for _, item := range arr {
1092					if m, ok := item.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
1093						if m["type"] == "text" {
1094							if text, ok := m["text"].(string); ok {
1095								texts = append(texts, text)
1096							}
1097						}
1098					}
1099				}
1100				if len(texts) > 0 {
1101					cleaned := textutil.StripIDEContextTags(strings.Join(texts, "\n\n"))
1102					if cleaned != "" {
1103						prompts = append(prompts, cleaned)
1104					}
1105				}
1106			}
1107		}
1108		return prompts
1109	}

1111	// splitPromptContent splits prompt.txt content on the "\n\n---\n\n" separator.
1112	// Returns nil if content is empty.
1113	func splitPromptContent(content string) []string {
1114		if content == "" {
1115			return nil
1116		}
1117		parts := strings.Split(content, "\n\n---\n\n")
1118		var result []string
1119		for _, p := range parts {
1120			trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(p)
1121			if trimmed != "" {
1122				result = append(result, trimmed)
1123			}
1124		}
1125		return result
1126	}

1156	// CondenseSessionByID condenses a session by its ID and cleans up.
1157	// This is used by "entire doctor" to salvage stuck sessions.
1158	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSessionByID(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) error {
1159		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "condense-by-id")
1160	
1161		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
1162		if err != nil {
1163			return fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
1164		}
1165		defer repo.Close()
1166	
1167		checkpointID, err := id.Generate()
1168		if err != nil {
1169			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
1170		}
1171	
1172		var shadowBranchName string
1173		var clearAfter bool
1174		mutErr := MutateSessionState(ctx, sessionID, func(state *SessionState) error {
1175			shadowBranchName = getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
1176			refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
1177			_, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true)
1178			hasShadowBranch := refErr == nil
1179	
1180			if !hasShadowBranch {
1181				logging.Info(logCtx, "no shadow branch for session, clearing state only",
1182					slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
1183					slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
1184				)
1185				clearAfter = true
1186				return ErrMutationSkip
1187			}
1188	
1189			result, err := s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, checkpointID, state, nil)
1190			if err != nil {
1191				return fmt.Errorf("failed to condense session: %w", err)
1192			}
1193	
1194			if result.Skipped {
1195				logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensation skipped (no transcript or files), marking fully condensed",
1196					slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
1197				)
1198				state.FullyCondensed = true
1199				return nil
1200			}
1201	
1202			logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensed by ID",
1203				slog.String("session_id", sessionID),

1357	// cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused deletes a shadow branch if no other active sessions reference it.
1358	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused(ctx context.Context, _ *git.Repository, shadowBranchName, excludeSessionID string) error {
1359		// List all session states to check if any other session uses this shadow branch
1360		allStates, err := s.listAllSessionStates(ctx)
1361		if err != nil {
1362			return fmt.Errorf("failed to list session states: %w", err)
1363		}
1364	
1365		for _, state := range allStates {
1366			if state.SessionID == excludeSessionID {
1367				continue
1368			}
1369			otherShadow := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
1370			if otherShadow == shadowBranchName && state.StepCount > 0 {
1371				// Another session still needs this shadow branch
1372				return nil
1373			}
1374		}
1375	
1376		// No other sessions need it, delete the shadow branch via CLI
1377		// (go-git v5's RemoveReference doesn't persist with packed refs/worktrees)
1378		if err := DeleteBranchCLI(ctx, shadowBranchName); err != nil {
1379			// Branch already gone is not an error
1380			if errors.Is(err, ErrBranchNotFound) {
1381				return nil
1382			}
1383			return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove shadow branch: %w", err)
1384		}
1385		return nil
1386	}

322		sessionIndex := s.findSessionIndex(ctx, basePath, existingSummary, entries, opts.SessionID)
323	
324		// Refuse if slot 0 already holds metadata for a DIFFERENT session ID.
325		// findSessionIndex only returns 0 when existingSummary is nil (fresh write)
326		// or when the summary claims slot 0 belongs to us — either way, the tree
327		// actually holding session-0 metadata for someone else is a corruption /
328		// stale-summary shape. Writing through it would overwrite data we don't
329		// know about. Bail instead of silently clobbering.
330		//
331		// We read and capture BEFORE writeSessionToSubdirectory clears the subtree,
332		// otherwise we'd only ever see our own write.
333		if sessionIndex == 0 {
334			if entry, exists := entries[fmt.Sprintf("%s0/%s", basePath, paths.MetadataFileName)]; exists {
335				if existingMeta, readErr := s.readMetadataFromBlob(entry.Hash); readErr == nil && existingMeta.SessionID != opts.SessionID {
336					logging.Error(ctx, "refusing checkpoint write: session 0 holds a different sessionID",
337						slog.String("checkpoint_id", opts.CheckpointID.String()),
338						slog.String("existing_session_id", existingMeta.SessionID),
339						slog.String("write_session_id", opts.SessionID),
340						slog.Bool("existing_summary_nil", existingSummary == nil))
341					return fmt.Errorf(
342						"refusing to overwrite session 0 of checkpoint %s: existing session ID %q differs from write session ID %q. The checkpoint tree is inconsistent (session 0 belongs to a different session than this write claims). No automated repair exists for this shape — please report it along with the output of `git ls-tree entire/checkpoints/v1 %s/`",
343						opts.CheckpointID, existingMeta.SessionID, opts.SessionID, opts.CheckpointID.Path(),
344					)
345				}
346			}
347		}
348	
349		// Write session files to numbered subdirectory
350		sessionPath := fmt.Sprintf("%s%d/", basePath, sessionIndex)
351		sessionFilePaths, err := s.writeSessionToSubdirectory(ctx, opts, sessionPath, entries)
352		if err != nil {
353			return err
354		}
355	
356		// Copy additional metadata files from directory if specified (to session subdirectory)
357		if opts.MetadataDir != "" {
358			if err := s.copyMetadataDir(ctx, opts.MetadataDir, sessionPath, entries); err != nil {
359				return fmt.Errorf("failed to copy metadata directory: %w", err)
360			}
361		}
362	
363		// Build the sessions array
364		var sessions []SessionFilePaths
365		if existingSummary != nil {
366			sessions = make([]SessionFilePaths, max(len(existingSummary.Sessions), sessionIndex+1))
367			copy(sessions, existingSummary.Sessions)
368		} else {
369			sessions = make([]SessionFilePaths, 1)
370		}
371		sessions[sessionIndex] = sessionFilePaths
372	
373		// Tripwire: an unreproduced production report had session 0 silently
374		// replaced with a different sessionID's data. The symptom was
375		// findSessionIndex returning 0 when it should have returned N
376		// (append). That happens if existingSummary is nil — yet the
377		// on-disk tree clearly had session 0's metadata. If we're writing
378		// at sessionIndex=0 while entries has pre-existing session-0
379		// metadata with a DIFFERENT sessionID, that's the exact bug shape.
380		// Loud WARN so we get a log trace instead of only the symptom.
381		if sessionIndex == 0 {
382			path := fmt.Sprintf("%s0/%s", basePath, paths.MetadataFileName)
383			if entry, exists := entries[path]; exists {
384				if existingMeta, readErr := s.readMetadataFromBlob(entry.Hash); readErr == nil && existingMeta.SessionID != opts.SessionID {
385					logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint write overwrites session 0 with a different sessionID — potential overwrite regression",
386						slog.String("checkpoint_id", opts.CheckpointID.String()),
387						slog.String("existing_session_id", existingMeta.SessionID),
388						slog.String("write_session_id", opts.SessionID),
389						slog.Bool("existing_summary_nil", existingSummary == nil))
390				}
391			}
392		}
393	
394		// Update root metadata.json with CheckpointSummary
395		return s.writeCheckpointSummary(opts, basePath, entries, sessions)
396	}

398	// writeSessionToSubdirectory writes a single session's files to a numbered subdirectory.
399	// Returns the absolute file paths from the git tree root for the sessions map.
400	func (s *GitStore) writeSessionToSubdirectory(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions, sessionPath string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (SessionFilePaths, error) {
401		filePaths := SessionFilePaths{}
402	
403		// Clear any existing entries at this path so stale files from a previous
404		// write (e.g. prompt.txt) don't persist on overwrite.
405		for key := range entries {
406			if strings.HasPrefix(key, sessionPath) {
407				delete(entries, key)
408			}
409		}
410	
411		// Write transcript
412		wroteTranscript, err := s.writeTranscript(ctx, opts, sessionPath, entries)
413		if err != nil {
414			return filePaths, err
415		}
416		if wroteTranscript {
417			filePaths.Transcript = "/" + sessionPath + paths.TranscriptFileName
418			filePaths.ContentHash = "/" + sessionPath + paths.ContentHashFileName
419		}
420	
421		// Write prompts via the 7-layer pipeline. OPF runs only in the
422		// pre-push rewrite path (manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go).
423		if len(opts.Prompts) > 0 {
424			promptContent := redactedJoinedPrompts(opts.Prompts)
425			blobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(promptContent))
426			if err != nil {
427				return filePaths, err
428			}
429			entries[sessionPath+paths.PromptFileName] = object.TreeEntry{
430				Name: sessionPath + paths.PromptFileName,
431				Mode: filemode.Regular,
432				Hash: blobHash,
433			}
434			filePaths.Prompt = "/" + sessionPath + paths.PromptFileName
435		}
436	
437		// Write session-level metadata.json (CommittedMetadata with all fields including initial_attribution)
438		sessionMetadata := CommittedMetadata{
439			CheckpointID:                opts.CheckpointID,
440			SessionID:                   opts.SessionID,
441			Strategy:                    opts.Strategy,
442			CreatedAt:                   checkpointCreatedAt(opts),
443			Branch:                      opts.Branch,
444			CheckpointsCount:            opts.CheckpointsCount,
445			FilesTouched:                opts.FilesTouched,
446			Agent:                       opts.Agent,
447			Model:                       opts.Model,
448			TurnID:                      opts.TurnID,
449			IsTask:                      opts.IsTask,
450			ToolUseID:                   opts.ToolUseID,
451			TranscriptIdentifierAtStart: opts.TranscriptIdentifierAtStart,
452			CheckpointTranscriptStart:   opts.CheckpointTranscriptStart,
453			TranscriptLinesAtStart:      opts.CheckpointTranscriptStart, // Deprecated: kept for backward compat
454			TokenUsage:                  opts.TokenUsage,
455			SkillEventsVersion:          skillEventsVersion(opts.SkillEvents),
456			SkillEvents:                 opts.SkillEvents,
457			SessionMetrics:              opts.SessionMetrics,
458			InitialAttribution:          opts.InitialAttribution,
459			PromptAttributions:          opts.PromptAttributionsJSON,
460			Summary:                     redactSummary(opts.Summary),
461			CLIVersion:                  versioninfo.Version,
462			Kind:                        opts.Kind,
463			ReviewSkills:                opts.ReviewSkills,
464			ReviewPrompt:                opts.ReviewPrompt,
465			InvestigateRunID:            opts.InvestigateRunID,
466			InvestigateTopic:            opts.InvestigateTopic,
467		}
468	
469		metadataJSON, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(sessionMetadata, "", "  ")
470		if err != nil {
471			return filePaths, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session metadata: %w", err)
472		}
473		metadataHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, metadataJSON)
474		if err != nil {
475			return filePaths, err
476		}
477		entries[sessionPath+paths.MetadataFileName] = object.TreeEntry{
478			Name: sessionPath + paths.MetadataFileName,
479			Mode: filemode.Regular,
480			Hash: metadataHash,
481		}
482		filePaths.Metadata = "/" + sessionPath + paths.MetadataFileName
483	
484		return filePaths, nil
485	}

487	// writeCheckpointSummary writes the root-level CheckpointSummary with aggregated statistics.
488	// sessions is the complete sessions array (already built by the caller).
489	func (s *GitStore) writeCheckpointSummary(opts WriteCommittedOptions, basePath string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry, sessions []SessionFilePaths) error {
490		checkpointsCount, filesTouched, tokenUsage, err := s.reaggregateFromEntries(basePath, len(sessions), entries)
491		if err != nil {
492			return fmt.Errorf("failed to aggregate session stats: %w", err)
493		}
494	
495		combinedAttribution := opts.CombinedAttribution
496		hasReview := opts.HasReview
497		hasInvestigation := opts.HasInvestigation
498		rootMetadataPath := basePath + paths.MetadataFileName
499		if entry, exists := entries[rootMetadataPath]; exists {
500			existingSummary, readErr := s.readSummaryFromBlob(entry.Hash)
501			if readErr == nil {
502				if combinedAttribution == nil {
503					combinedAttribution = existingSummary.CombinedAttribution
504				}
505				if !hasReview {
506					hasReview = existingSummary.HasReview
507				}
508				if !hasInvestigation {
509					hasInvestigation = existingSummary.HasInvestigation
510				}
511			}
512		}
513	
514		summary := CheckpointSummary{
515			CheckpointID:        opts.CheckpointID,
516			CLIVersion:          versioninfo.Version,
517			Strategy:            opts.Strategy,
518			Branch:              opts.Branch,
519			CheckpointsCount:    checkpointsCount,
520			FilesTouched:        filesTouched,
521			Sessions:            sessions,
522			TokenUsage:          tokenUsage,
523			CombinedAttribution: combinedAttribution,
524			HasReview:           hasReview,
525			HasInvestigation:    hasInvestigation,
526		}
527	
528		metadataJSON, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(summary, "", "  ")
529		if err != nil {
530			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal checkpoint summary: %w", err)
531		}
532		metadataHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, metadataJSON)
533		if err != nil {
534			return err
535		}
536		entries[basePath+paths.MetadataFileName] = object.TreeEntry{
537			Name: basePath + paths.MetadataFileName,
538			Mode: filemode.Regular,
539			Hash: metadataHash,
540		}
541		return nil
542	}

544	// UpdateCheckpointSummary updates root-level checkpoint metadata fields that depend
545	// on the full set of sessions already written to the checkpoint.
546	func (s *GitStore) UpdateCheckpointSummary(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, combinedAttribution *InitialAttribution) error {
547		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
548			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // Propagating context cancellation
549		}
550	
551		if err := s.ensureSessionsBranch(ctx); err != nil {
552			return fmt.Errorf("failed to ensure sessions branch: %w", err)
553		}
554	
555		parentHash, rootTreeHash, err := s.getSessionsBranchRef()
556		if err != nil {
557			return err
558		}
559	
560		basePath := checkpointID.Path() + "/"
561		checkpointPath := checkpointID.Path()
562		entries, err := s.flattenCheckpointEntries(rootTreeHash, checkpointPath)
563		if err != nil {
564			return err
565		}
566	
567		rootMetadataPath := basePath + paths.MetadataFileName
568		entry, exists := entries[rootMetadataPath]
569		if !exists {
570			return ErrCheckpointNotFound
571		}
572	
573		summary, err := s.readSummaryFromBlob(entry.Hash)
574		if err != nil {
575			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read checkpoint summary: %w", err)
576		}
577		summary.CombinedAttribution = combinedAttribution
578	
579		metadataJSON, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(summary, "", "  ")
580		if err != nil {
581			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal checkpoint summary: %w", err)
582		}
583		metadataHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, metadataJSON)
584		if err != nil {
585			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create checkpoint summary blob: %w", err)
586		}
587		entries[rootMetadataPath] = object.TreeEntry{
588			Name: rootMetadataPath,
589			Mode: filemode.Regular,
590			Hash: metadataHash,
591		}
592	
593		newTreeHash, err := s.spliceCheckpointSubtree(ctx, rootTreeHash, checkpointID, basePath, entries)
594		if err != nil {
595			return err
596		}
597	
598		authorName, authorEmail := GetGitAuthorFromRepo(s.repo)
599		commitMsg := fmt.Sprintf("Update checkpoint summary for %s", checkpointID)
600		newCommitHash, err := s.createCommit(ctx, newTreeHash, parentHash, commitMsg, authorName, authorEmail)
601		if err != nil {
602			return err
603		}
604	
605		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
606		newRef := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, newCommitHash)
607		if err := s.repo.Storer.SetReference(newRef); err != nil {
608			return fmt.Errorf("failed to set branch reference: %w", err)
609		}
610	
611		return nil
612	}

614	// findSessionIndex returns the index of an existing session with the given ID,
615	// or the next available index if not found. This prevents duplicate session entries.
616	func (s *GitStore) findSessionIndex(ctx context.Context, basePath string, existingSummary *CheckpointSummary, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry, sessionID string) int {
617		if existingSummary == nil {
618			return 0
619		}
620		for i := range len(existingSummary.Sessions) {
621			path := fmt.Sprintf("%s%d/%s", basePath, i, paths.MetadataFileName)
622			entry, exists := entries[path]
623			if !exists {
624				continue
625			}
626			meta, err := s.readMetadataFromBlob(entry.Hash)
627			if err != nil {
628				logging.Warn(ctx, "failed to read session metadata during dedup check",
629					slog.Int("session_index", i),
630					slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
631					slog.String("error", err.Error()),
632				)
633				continue
634			}
635			if meta.SessionID == sessionID {
636				return i
637			}
638		}
639		return len(existingSummary.Sessions)
640	}

642	// reaggregateFromEntries reads all session metadata from the entries map and
643	// reaggregates CheckpointsCount, FilesTouched, and TokenUsage.
644	func (s *GitStore) reaggregateFromEntries(basePath string, sessionCount int, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (int, []string, *agent.TokenUsage, error) {
645		var totalCount int
646		var allFiles []string
647		var totalTokens *agent.TokenUsage
648	
649		for i := range sessionCount {
650			path := fmt.Sprintf("%s%d/%s", basePath, i, paths.MetadataFileName)
651			entry, exists := entries[path]
652			if !exists {
653				return 0, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("session %d metadata not found at %s", i, path)
654			}
655			meta, err := s.readMetadataFromBlob(entry.Hash)
656			if err != nil {
657				return 0, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session %d metadata: %w", i, err)
658			}
659			totalCount += meta.CheckpointsCount
660			allFiles = mergeFilesTouched(allFiles, meta.FilesTouched)
661			totalTokens = aggregateTokenUsage(totalTokens, meta.TokenUsage)
662		}
663	
664		return totalCount, allFiles, totalTokens, nil
665	}

681	// readJSONFromBlob reads JSON from a blob hash and decodes it to the given type.
682	func readJSONFromBlob[T any](repo *git.Repository, hash plumbing.Hash) (*T, error) {
683		blob, err := repo.BlobObject(hash)
684		if err != nil {
685			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get blob: %w", err)
686		}
687	
688		reader, err := blob.Reader()
689		if err != nil {
690			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get blob reader: %w", err)
691		}
692		defer reader.Close()
693	
694		var result T
695		if err := json.NewDecoder(reader).Decode(&result); err != nil {
696			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode: %w", err)
697		}
698	
699		return &result, nil
700	}

707	// aggregateTokenUsage sums two TokenUsage structs.
708	// Returns nil if both inputs are nil.
709	func aggregateTokenUsage(a, b *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
710		if a == nil && b == nil {
711			return nil
712		}
713		result := &agent.TokenUsage{}
714		if a != nil {
715			result.InputTokens = a.InputTokens
716			result.CacheCreationTokens = a.CacheCreationTokens
717			result.CacheReadTokens = a.CacheReadTokens
718			result.OutputTokens = a.OutputTokens
719			result.APICallCount = a.APICallCount
720		}
721		if b != nil {
722			result.InputTokens += b.InputTokens
723			result.CacheCreationTokens += b.CacheCreationTokens
724			result.CacheReadTokens += b.CacheReadTokens
725			result.OutputTokens += b.OutputTokens
726			result.APICallCount += b.APICallCount
727		}
728		return result
729	}

731	// writeTranscript writes the transcript and content hash to the checkpoint entries.
732	// Returns (true, nil) if files were written, (false, nil) if transcript was empty.
733	func (s *GitStore) writeTranscript(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions, basePath string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (bool, error) {
734		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
735		transcriptBytes := opts.Transcript.Bytes()
736	
737		// TranscriptPath fallback: data read from disk is an untrusted source,
738		// so we redact it here. The in-memory path (opts.Transcript) is already
739		// pre-redacted by the caller — enforced by the RedactedBytes type.
740		if len(transcriptBytes) == 0 && opts.TranscriptPath != "" {
741			rawData, readErr := os.ReadFile(opts.TranscriptPath)
742			if readErr != nil {
743				// Non-fatal: transcript may not exist yet
744				rawData = nil
745			}
746			if len(rawData) > 0 {
747				redacted, redactErr := redact.JSONLBytes(rawData)
748				if redactErr != nil {
749					return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to redact transcript from file: %w", redactErr)
750				}
751				transcriptBytes = redacted.Bytes()
752			}
753		}
754		if len(transcriptBytes) == 0 {
755			return false, nil
756		}
757	
758		if opts.Agent == agent.AgentTypeCodex {
759			transcriptBytes = codex.SanitizePortableTranscript(transcriptBytes)
760		}
761	
762		// Chunk the transcript if it's too large
763		chunkStart := time.Now()
764		chunkCtx, chunkTranscriptSpan := perf.Start(ctx, "chunk_transcript")
765		chunks, err := agent.ChunkTranscript(chunkCtx, transcriptBytes, opts.Agent)
766		if err != nil {
767			chunkTranscriptSpan.RecordError(err)
768			chunkTranscriptSpan.End()
769			return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to chunk transcript: %w", err)
770		}
771		chunkTranscriptSpan.End()
772		chunkDuration := time.Since(chunkStart)
773	
774		// Write chunk files
775		blobStart := time.Now()
776		blobCtx, writeTranscriptBlobsSpan := perf.Start(chunkCtx, "write_transcript_blobs")
777		for i, chunk := range chunks {
778			chunkPath := basePath + agent.ChunkFileName(paths.TranscriptFileName, i)
779			blobHash, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, chunk)
780			if err != nil {
781				writeTranscriptBlobsSpan.RecordError(err)
782				writeTranscriptBlobsSpan.End()
783				return false, err
784			}
785			entries[chunkPath] = object.TreeEntry{
786				Name: chunkPath,
787				Mode: filemode.Regular,
788				Hash: blobHash,
789			}
790		}
791		writeTranscriptBlobsSpan.End()
792		blobDuration := time.Since(blobStart)
793	
794		// Content hash for deduplication (hash of full transcript)
795		contentHashStart := time.Now()
796		_, contentHashSpan := perf.Start(blobCtx, "write_transcript_content_hash")
797		contentHash := fmt.Sprintf("sha256:%x", sha256.Sum256(transcriptBytes))
798		hashBlob, err := CreateBlobFromContent(s.repo, []byte(contentHash))
799		if err != nil {
800			contentHashSpan.RecordError(err)
801			contentHashSpan.End()
802			return false, err
803		}
804		entries[basePath+paths.ContentHashFileName] = object.TreeEntry{
805			Name: basePath + paths.ContentHashFileName,
806			Mode: filemode.Regular,
807			Hash: hashBlob,
808		}
809		contentHashSpan.End()
810	
811		logging.Debug(logCtx, "write transcript timings",
812			slog.String("session_id", opts.SessionID),
813			slog.String("checkpoint_id", opts.CheckpointID.String()),
814			slog.String("agent", string(opts.Agent)),
815			slog.Int64("chunk_transcript_ms", chunkDuration.Milliseconds()),
816			slog.Int64("write_transcript_blobs_ms", blobDuration.Milliseconds()),
817			slog.Int64("write_transcript_content_hash_ms", time.Since(contentHashStart).Milliseconds()),
818			slog.Int("transcript_bytes", len(transcriptBytes)),
819			slog.Int("chunk_count", len(chunks)),
820		)
821		return true, nil
822	}

824	// mergeFilesTouched combines two file lists, removing duplicates.
825	// All paths are normalized to forward slashes for platform-agnostic storage.
826	func mergeFilesTouched(existing, additional []string) []string {
827		seen := make(map[string]bool)
828		var result []string
829	
830		for _, f := range existing {
831			f = filepath.ToSlash(f)
832			if !seen[f] {
833				seen[f] = true
834				result = append(result, f)
835			}
836		}
837		for _, f := range additional {
838			f = filepath.ToSlash(f)
839			if !seen[f] {
840				seen[f] = true
841				result = append(result, f)
842			}
843		}
844	
845		sort.Strings(result)
846		return result
847	}
